subject: MAP: Performance evaluation & regional failover summary
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Chan <olivia@acmecloud.com>, Ben Turner <ben.turner@acmecloud.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-03T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: MAP kickoff: Performance evaluation plan (latency, throughput, failover)

Hi Olivia / Ben —

Thanks for agreeing to the MAP workshop last week. As discussed, we want to fold a short but measurable performance evaluation into the MAP so AcmeCloud can validate SLAs for your latency-sensitive search use-case before contract close. Draft plan below — please confirm scope and timing.

Scope
- Test surfaces: generation endpoint (chat/text), embeddings route for indexing, and the routing layer for multi-region failover.
- Metrics: p50/p95/p99 latencies (ms), TTFT (time-to-first-token), steady-state throughput (tokens/sec), end-to-end concurrency behavior, and failover detection/recovery times across US/EU/APAC.
- Workload profiles: 3 profiles (search short prompts, conversational medium prompts ~120 tokens, bulk indexing ~1k tokens).

Timing (proposed)
- Baseline run (US region): 2026-05-06 — smoke + single-region throughput curve
- Multi-region latency sweep: 2026-05-07 — distributed clients from EU/APAC to measure routing and geo latency
- Failover + routing test: 2026-05-08 — simulate AZ/region outage and measure switchover and TTFT impact
- Delivery of results and MAP update: 2026-05-10

Deliverables
- CSV of raw traces and summary metrics (p50/p95/p99, throughput at target concurrencies).
- Short slide deck with callouts/recommendations (batching/quantization profiles, suggested routing policy).
- MAP updated with final acceptance criteria and signoffs.

Action items for AcmeCloud
- Confirm traffic sample for short/medium/long profiles (JSON or sample log) by 2026-05-04.
- Approve test windows and provide VIP test endpoints if available.

Internal: Karthik & Rafael — can you confirm available test harness and whether we need additional infra (e.g., ephemeral clients in APAC)? Marissa, tagging you for the MAP doc template and signoff workflow.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.ai

Date: 2026-05-04T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff: Performance evaluation plan (latency, throughput, failover) — test harness and metrics

Laura / team —

Confirming test harness and measurement definitions so AcmeCloud knows what to expect. Short summary:

Test harness
- Redwood load generator (rg-load) with scripted client geo-distribution. Will run from ephemeral clients in us-east-1, eu-west-1, and ap-southeast-1.
- Each test pass = 10-minute ramp, 20-minute steady window, 10-minute ramp down.
- For concurrency curves we'll sweep target concurrent connections: 8, 16, 32, 64, 128.

Metrics definitions
- p95 latency = 95th percentile end-to-end server response time (ms) measured at Redwood edge before streaming splits.
- TTFT = time from request accepted by front-door to first token emitted by model (ms). We'll record cold vs warm (cache hit on KV).
- Throughput = tokens/sec (aggregate) during steady window; measured both per-node and cluster-wide.
- Failover detection time = time between simulated route outage and DNS/routing convergence (ms) + time to first successful token on fallback model/region.

Artifacts
- Raw traces (CSV), aggregated metrics (CSV), an execution trace for failover (JSON).

Rafael — please run a dry run on 5/05 in our staging infrastructure to validate instrumentation. I will coordinate client VMs with Acme.

Karthik
Head, Platform Reliability | Redwood Inference

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Olivia Chan <olivia@acmecloud.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-08T14:36:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP: Performance evaluation & regional failover summary — results attached

Hi all —

We completed the planned runs (US baseline, multi-region sweep, and failover) and attached the raw traces. Summary highlights below — see attached CSV and failover trace for full numbers.

Key results (medium prompt ~120 tokens, 8k context disabled)
- US (us-east-1) baseline at concurrency=64: p50 28 ms, p95 72 ms, p99 210 ms; TTFT cold=180 ms, warm=48 ms; throughput steady = 11,200 tokens/sec cluster-wide.
- EU (eu-west-1) from EU clients (no routing): p95 88 ms; TTFT warm=62 ms.
- APAC (ap-southeast-1) from APAC clients: p95 130 ms; TTFT warm=95 ms.

Concurrency scaling (US region)
- 8 -> p95 ~35 ms; 16 -> p95 ~40 ms; 32 -> p95 ~55 ms; 64 -> p95 ~72 ms; 128 -> p95 ~160 ms (note visible tail growth).

Throughput notes (bulk / long profile ~1k tokens)
- Sustained token throughput dropped by ~12% on cold cache runs vs warmed runs; warmed runs achieved up to 9,400 tokens/sec on the bulk profile at concurrency=64.

Failover & routing observations
- Simulated region outage: we injected route blackhole for us-east-1 at t=13:05:00 UTC during a steady-state run. Detected by health checks and policy-based router after 4.2s; DNS TTL based routing took ~9s to converge for some client populations.
- Time to first successful token on fallback (EU region serving US client) averaged 1.3s with transient TTFT spike to ~1.9s on first request; subsequent requests returned to normal warm TTFT.
- Multi-region routing (latency-based policy) routed ~87% of US-origin requests to us-east as expected, but during simulated load spike we observed spillover to us-west which increased p95 by ~40 ms for those few connections.

Recommendations
- For AcmeCloud search SLA (p95 < 100 ms target), enable regional edge caching and prefer latency-based routing pinned to US/eu endpoints with a sub-5s failover threshold.
- Consider conservative concurrency soft limits (<=64) at peak to avoid tail spikes; auto-scale buffers for bursts.
- Add a quick warmup policy for bulk index jobs (pre-warm KV cache) to reduce cold TTFT impact.

Attachments
- 20260510_acme_latency_results.csv (raw traces + aggregates)
- failover_trace_us-eu-apac.json (execution trace)

Questions / next steps
- Laura: propose we slot a 30-min review with Acme next week and fold the acceptance criteria into the MAP. If Acme agrees, we can move to signature and aim to close by 2026-05-24 (per MAP timeline).

Rafael Mendes
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
rafael_mendes@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: MAP: Performance evaluation & regional failover summary — final MAP updates & close timeline

Olivia / Ben —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and for providing test endpoints. Rafael and Karthik's runs gave us what we need to make an acceptance call. I've updated the MAP with the acceptance criteria and owner assignments (attached). High-level MAP items and dates below:

Mutual Action Plan (summary)
1) Performance acceptance criteria — Acme to confirm: p95 <= 100 ms for search medium profile in US with <=64 concurrency; TTFT warm <=70 ms. Owner: Olivia — due 2026-05-12.
2) Routing & failover policy — Redwood to provision latency-based routing with 4s health-check detection and a 10s DNS convergence fallback. Owner: Karthik / Rafael — actioned, ETA 2026-05-14.
3) Pre-warm policy for bulk indexing — Redwood to provide quick warmup script and map it into job orchestration. Owner: Rafael — ETA 2026-05-16.
4) Legal & procurement final terms (pricing, support levels) — Acme procurement and Redwood sales to finalize. Owner: Ben / Laura — target signature 2026-05-24.

Next steps
- Schedule 30-min technical review with Acme (I propose 2026-05-13 10:00 PT). Please confirm availability.
- Once Olivia confirms acceptance criteria by 5/12 we will mark the MAP as "ready for legal" and move toward signature.

If these dates look good I will update the HubSpot deal and send the MAP doc for electronic signoff.

Thanks — close timeline looks feasible if we get the acceptance sign by 5/12.

Laura Bennett
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
